unlisted_practices: Regulatory and HTA bodies should develop category-specific frameworks and guidelines for digital health technologies and digital health services.
Regulatory and HTA bodies should require developers of LLM-embedded digital health technologies to transparently outline strategies to mitigate bias in their models.
Regulatory and HTA bodies should require LLM developers to disclose methods for managing the generation of misleading information and for addressing data security and patient privacy concerns.

Regulatory and HTA bodies should develop new assessment methods to evaluate accuracy, intended and unintended effects on patient outcomes, continuous monitoring, and rigorous testing of digital health solutions.

Regulatory and HTA bodies should specify requirements for LLMs used in digital health technologies, including clinical validation studies, risk-benefit analysis, privacy safeguards, security measures, performance metrics, usability criteria, interoperability standards, and post-market surveillance.
Health systems should ensure digital health technologies meet defined requirements and evaluate their real-world performance.
Use digital health and AI terminology accurately and distinctly and avoid treating them as interchangeable.
Involve healthcare providers, clinical experts, patients, AI developers, and regulatory and reimbursement authorities collaboratively in developing and implementing AI and digital health frameworks.

screen.reason: Commentary discussing definitions, categorization, and regulatory/HTA framework requirements for digital health technologies and AI in healthcare.
